pointOnCubic3.internal: Bezier evaluation for the gear outlines; public curve evaluation is decided with the curves package

PARALLEL_SINE.internal: a tolerance the frame checks share, not an operation

WORLD_AXES.internal: a constant, the world's own axes

axesAlong.internal: how a mesh primitive stands on a direction alone; a public frame takes the X direction its caller chooses (`frame.create`)

isFrameShaped.internal: an input guard the services run on what they are given

isTriple.internal: an input guard the services run on what they are given

unitOf.internal: the 3D tuple form of `vector.normalized` for hot paths

checkedUnitOfLength.internal: the input guard every unit-aware method runs on its `unit`, before `math.millimetresPerUnit` would see a value outside the enum

lengthsConverted.internal: the per-field form of `math.convertLength` the engineering tables convert their results with

snappedLength.internal: a table's length converted into the caller's unit, rounded so the conversion leaves no float noise

tableLength.internal: a caller's length converted into a table's own unit and rounded to the table's resolution, so a size rounded in another unit still matches its row

followedBy.internal: the two-matrix step `transforms.combine` folds a list with

isTransformMatrix.internal: an input guard the services run on what they are given

movedCoordinate.internal: the affine tuple and buffer forms of `point.transformPoint` for hot paths; `point.transformPoint` also divides by w

movedPoint.internal: the affine tuple and buffer forms of `point.transformPoint` for hot paths; `point.transformPoint` also divides by w

movedPositions.internal: the affine tuple and buffer forms of `point.transformPoint` for hot paths; `point.transformPoint` also divides by w

symmetricEigen.internal: the solve behind `frame.bestFit`; a general linear-algebra API is outside base

turnedVector.internal: the affine tuple and buffer forms of `point.transformPoint` for hot paths; `point.transformPoint` also divides by w

roundedToMillionths.internal: the six places the engineering size tables are rounded to; `math.roundToDecimals` is the general form

add2.internal: the fixed-size tuple form of `vector.add` for hot paths; `vector.add` takes vectors of any length

add3.internal: the fixed-size tuple form of `vector.add` for hot paths; `vector.add` takes vectors of any length

between2.internal: interpolation from `a` toward `b` for hot paths; public as `vector.lerp`, which weighs `first` by `fraction`, so its operands run the other way

between3.internal: interpolation from `a` toward `b` for hot paths; public as `vector.lerp`, which weighs `first` by `fraction`, so its operands run the other way

cross2.internal: the plan form of `vector.cross` for hot paths: the turn from one plan direction to another

distance2.internal: the plan tuple form of `point.distance` for hot paths

distance3.internal: the tuple form of `point.distance` for hot paths

dot2.internal: the fixed-size tuple form of `vector.dot` for hot paths; `vector.dot` takes vectors of any length

dot3.internal: the fixed-size tuple form of `vector.dot` for hot paths; `vector.dot` takes vectors of any length

leftOf2.internal: a plan quarter turn the outline code uses on hot paths; `point.rotatePointsCenterAxis` turns by any angle

length2.internal: the plan tuple form of `vector.length` for hot paths; `vector.length` takes a vector in space

polar2.internal: the plan, radian tuple form of `frame.polar` for hot paths

rotated2.internal: the plan, radian tuple form of `point.rotatePointsCenterAxis` about z for hot paths

scale2.internal: the fixed-size tuple form of `vector.mul` for hot paths; `vector.mul` takes vectors of any length

scale3.internal: the fixed-size tuple form of `vector.mul` for hot paths; `vector.mul` takes vectors of any length

subtract2.internal: the fixed-size tuple form of `vector.sub` for hot paths; `vector.sub` takes vectors of any length

subtract3.internal: the fixed-size tuple form of `vector.sub` for hot paths; `vector.sub` takes vectors of any length

unit2Of.internal: the plan tuple form of `vector.normalized` for hot paths, scaled as `unitOf` is so a plan direction normalises to the bits it has in space

creasedMesh.internal: the drawers' single-precision form of `creasedVertices`, with the positions written out for the GPU

pointOnTree.internal: the clash check's choice of points for its inside test, not a building block

pointsOnTree.internal: the clash check's choice of points for its inside test, not a building block

treeBox.internal: the box of a tree, read by the tree queries

triangleTree.internal: the acceleration structure the mesh queries build; users ask the query, not for the tree
